clue.text: Colony which pays off

definitions.meaning: a group of settlers and the place they have founded
a payment that clears a debt or resolves a dispute between parties

explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a new community of settlers, and a final payment agreed to end a claim also carries the same name.

clue.text: Go for booty and get the boot!

definitions.meaning: to plunder a captured town for its loot
to be dismissed from a job, kicked out

explanation.definitionFit: To pillage a city and to be fired from work share one short verb, the second sense an informal idiom for dismissal.

clue.text: It is up to me for a while

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that is up has been written from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declaring that a decision rests with them, at least for now.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is up' reverses the first word; 'to' is only a link, and 'for' introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A while is a period or stretch of duration, a span of the clock.

clue.text: 51 isle-scattered flowers

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: letters scattered about are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Blooms strewn over some island, with an odd number attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals are a crossword staple; the hyphen in 'isle-scattered' hides that 'scattered' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilies are tall trumpet-shaped blooms, a kind of plant prized in gardens.

clue.text: The doorman outside is being cautious?

definitions.text: The doorman outside is being cautious?

parts.words: The doorman outside is being cautious?
parts.note: a doorman stationed outside a building literally looks after its front step, while the phrase also means treading carefully

explanation.definitionFit: Watching where you put your feet is an idiom for acting with care, and a porter literally tends a doorstep.

clue.text: Snuggle down in finest leather

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the two

explanation.surface: Curling up cosily wrapped in the best hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle comfortably close against something, a synonym of snuggling.

clue.text: No base for a police unit

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A police squad left without a headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry an acid is the opposite of a base (alkali), so 'No base' is a fair definition; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry acids and alkalis are opposites, so a substance that is not alkaline is the other kind.

clue.text: Understanding magnetic in, instrument with electric charge

parts.note: a compass is a navigational instrument, the magnetic kind with a needle
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Grasping how a magnetic device works with power applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magnetic' describes the instrument; the 'in,' appears to be an OCR stray and is read as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is sympathetic understanding of another's suffering, a fellow feeling.

clue.text: Roy deserts wrecked naval vessels

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man named Roy abandons ships that have been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroyers are fast warships used by navies, a class of fighting ship.

clue.text: Beauty comes with deep wrinkles

indicators.note: here 'with' means carrying inside, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: lines are creases in the skin

explanation.surface: Ageing brings good looks along with its deep creases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a mere link, but here it means holding, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Comeliness is attractiveness, an old-fashioned word for good looks.

clue.text: The whole body turned to a prophet

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for the body is read from its end back

parts.note: soma is the body of an organism as a whole, as distinct from the mind or germ cells

explanation.surface: A congregation wholly converted to following a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor Old Testament prophets, with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: Thrusting forth scar shows anything but humble spirit

parts.note: the opposite of humble is proud
flesh is traditionally set against spirit, as body against soul, the contrast continuing 'anything but'

explanation.surface: An arrogant person's swagger described as anything but meek.
explanation.walkthrough: Proud flesh is the swollen granulation tissue that pushes up round a healing wound; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically, raised granulation tissue that bulges out of a wound as it heals is given this name.

clue.text: No light stopped play

definitions.meaning: a cricket pitch too dark to play on, as when bad light stops play

explanation.definitionFit: Utter darkness is described as this, and in cricket a pitch too dark for play halts the game.

clue.text: They serve humans with different ails

parts.note: men is a word for people in general

indicators.note: different here means changed, so these letters take another order

explanation.surface: Servants are people with assorted complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They serve' looks like a description of humans; it is the definition, servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Menials are domestic servants or those doing lowly work for others.

clue.text: Must have been under-treated under a doctor

definitions.text: Must have been under-treated under a doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece written under another follows it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: treated means processed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient who got too little care from the physician did not survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges UNDER into URNED, which goes beneath MO. The whole clue suggests why someone was grieved for.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient so neglected must have died and been grieved for, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Pedestrian vehicle

parts.note: a ride propelled by pushing a foot against the ground, so it is powered on foot like a walker

explanation.definitionFit: A child's kick-board on wheels is pushed along by foot, so it is a transport for someone on foot.

clue.text: Horn is carved-from which animals?

indicators.note: carved up, so these letters are cut and reshaped

explanation.surface: A question about which beasts a carved horn came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' rearranges HORNIS; the horn is the very thing those beasts are hunted for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinos are large thick-skinned African and Asian mammals with horns on the snout.

clue.text: East Central den supplies tasty pastry

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
C is an abbreviation for central
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A bakery in some eastern district selling cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a long choux bun filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: International ritual admits debts of 50 casually

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is an international body

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a ceremony is a ritual
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A global rite lets in fifty debts without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' is the container signal and covers both the debts and the Roman fifty; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something abruptly and without formality or courtesy is acting offhandedly.

clue.text: Fit in Queen's title which is most famous

indicators.note: one word goes inside the abbreviation for the royal title

parts.note: FD, Fidei Defensor (Defender of the Faith), is a royal title printed on British coins
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A capable person given a royal honour becomes celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: FD (Defender of the Faith) appears on British coins after the monarch's name; 'which is most' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabled is celebrated in story and legend, renowned.

clue.text: Humourless nonsense may bring the house down

parts.note: dry means dull, lacking humour
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A dull comedian's rubbish might still win huge applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring the house down' looks like theatrical success; dry rot is a fungus that destroys timber and can wreck a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay of wood that can make a building collapse.

clue.text: Consume our 500 electrovolts first

indicators.note: first means these pieces come before the other one

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
eV is the symbol for electron volts

explanation.surface: A command to use up our supply of electrical energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to eat up greedily, a synonym of consuming.

clue.text: Hold up could mean arrest

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a person waiting and keeping a suspect in custody are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Theatre assistant found in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a person who helps actors with costumes
a sideboard with shelves for plates

explanation.definitionFit: A stage helper who clothes performers and a cupboard holding crockery share the name.

clue.text: Test for the PM?

parts.note: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is also a post-mortem, the medical inspection of a body after death

explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is a medical inspection, and the short form of that word means a test such as a school paper.

clue.text: Desert where I bog up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the pair is backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dry wasteland where someone sinks into a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Way you once got trouble with the blinkers

parts.note: ST is short for street
ye is an archaic word for you

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned road user having problems with a horse's eye shields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinkers' suggests a horse's eye shields or car indicators; here they are eyelids, and a stye is an eyelid swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an eye complaint.

clue.text: Pen commentary on a boxing match after the Western tradition

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the other one

parts.note: a rite is a traditional ceremony
a bout is a boxing contest

explanation.surface: Ringside reporting on a fight in the cowboy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To write about a subject is to put a commentary on it into words.

clue.text: Take a long walk if bomb gets Eisenhower

parts.note: H stands for the hydrogen bomb, the H-bomb
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go trekking should an atomic weapon reach the President.
explanation.definitionFit: A hike is a long country walk, and as a verb means to tramp.

clue.text: Stay at home before 2, then use brakes promptly

indicators.note: before means these pieces come ahead of the other

parts.note: to stop is to stay
in means at home
refers to the answer to clue 2, meaning a while

explanation.surface: Advice to a driver to stay home, then brake quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt a vehicle without delay before hitting something is to pull up in good season.
